_about: Stocks that keep their hand-written bear/base/bull scenarios (model/model.py STOCKS) instead of the rule-based ones (data/scenarios_rule.json). Every entry needs a written reason. Remove an entry to put the stock back on the rules.

AMZN.reason: Free cash flow is negative while it spends on AI data centres, so five years of cash margins say nothing about what the business earns once the build-out slows (rule bear case is below zero).

GOOGL.reason: AI capex has pushed the last-12-month cash margin below zero; the rule reads that as the new normal. Analysts' 28% growth is also outside what companies this size have done, so the rule cuts it to 10%.

LLY.reason: Cash margins of the last four years are depressed by plant building and bought-in research (two years below zero) during the GLP-1 ramp.

RDDT.reason: Only two profitable years: the five-year margin history is mostly start-up losses (rule base margin 0.3% vs 26% now).

XYZ.reason: Cash margin has climbed from -6% to 19% in four years; the history is mostly the loss-making years.

CRCL.reason: Listed in 2025; margins swing with interest rates and the history includes pre-listing losses. Analysts' 24% growth depends on stablecoin supply.

SHOP.reason: Margin history includes the 2022 logistics losses (-13%); margins since are 13-15% and rising.

WDAY.reason: Cash margin after stock pay has risen every year (0% to 12%) as stock pay shrinks relative to sales; the history understates where it is heading.

NVDA.reason: Analysts expect 68% growth and the last three years averaged 100%; no group of large companies in the base rates has done this, so the rule's number is not grounded. Hand scenarios stay deliberately lower.

AVGO.reason: Analysts expect 66% growth on AI chips; the base rates cut it to 12%, half the hand-written 25%. VMware also distorts the three-year history.

MRVL.reason: Analysts expect 64% growth on AI chips; the base rates cut it to 13%.

APP.reason: Sales growth of 25%+ with a 60% cash margin is outside the base rates for its size; the rule halves growth.

NRG.reason: Analysts' -2.5% is a change in how revenue is reported after the 2026 acquisitions, and cash flow swings with working capital; the rule reads both as a shrinking, low-margin business.

KO.reason: Analysts' -3% reflects selling bottling operations (refranchising), not weaker demand; two years of cash flow include a tax deposit and a deal payment.

IDCC.reason: Licensing revenue is lumpy: catch-up payments made 2022 and 2025 unusually high, and analysts' -13% is the fall back to normal.

FIS.reason: The Worldpay stake sale and the Issuer Solutions purchase change both revenue and cash flow in 2026; history and analysts' figures mix the old and new company.

NDAQ.reason: The Adenza purchase (late 2023) changed the margin: 36% now vs 22-23% before; the history is mostly the old company.

APA.reason: Sales follow oil and gas prices, not volumes: analysts' growth is a price forecast and margins are a price cycle.

EOG.reason: Sales follow oil and gas prices, not volumes: analysts' growth is a price forecast and margins are a price cycle.

CF.reason: Sales and margins follow nitrogen fertiliser and natural-gas prices; the five-year history includes the 2022 price spike.

NEM.reason: Sales and margins follow the gold price (three-year growth 24%, margin 0% to 37%); hand scenarios assume gold flat to lower.

CTRE.reason: Grows by buying properties, which free cash flow leaves out: the rule sees a 98% margin and 28% growth and nearly triples the value.

SPG.reason: Cash flow before property purchases and redevelopment overstates what owners keep; hand margin is set lower for that.

HST.reason: Cash flow before hotel purchases and renovations overstates what owners keep; hand margin is set lower for that.

MO.reason: Cigarette volumes fall every year; the rule's minimum long-run growth is 2.5%, the hand scenarios use 0%.

BMY.reason: Eliquis and Opdivo lose patent protection from 2028; past margins belong to drugs that are about to face generics.

INVA.reason: Most income is GSK royalties that run off in the 2030s; hand scenarios use 0% long-run growth, the rule 6.5%.

ADYEY.reason: US ADR figures converted from euros: the history shows -33% three-year growth and 95% margins (merchant money in cash flow), neither real.

FISV.reason: Guidance was reset in late 2025 and the cash margin fell to 13%; the five-year history (16-23%) belongs to the earlier business plan.
